notice: RN bank batch 150: Pediatric case studies: catch-up vaccines, infant meningitis, foreign body aspiration and lead poisoning, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: A child arrives at the emergency department with sudden breathing trouble. Using the note, fill in the bowtie: the most likely problem in the middle, two actions to take now on the left and two parameters to monitor on the right.

actions.text: Look in the throat with a tongue blade to see the epiglottis
Lay the child flat on the stretcher for a neck x-ray
Take a throat culture now before antibiotics start

rationale.correct: Drooling, tripod position and high fever in an unvaccinated child is epiglottitis; protect the airway.

perOption.c1: Sudden high fever, drooling, tripod position, muffled voice, unvaccinated.
perOption.c4: No choking episode and high fever.
perOption.a5: Wait until the airway is secure.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: 4-year-old, no Hib vaccine. Fever 40 C for 6 hours, drooling, sitting forward on the hands, muffled voice, soft stridor. Refuses to lie down.

questions.stem: For each age, choose Erikson's developmental task.

cells.text: Cries and is comforted by a consistent caregiver
Says "no" and wants to do things alone
Collects things, likes to finish projects
Tries out styles and values; peers matter most

rationale.correct: Erikson's stages guide age-appropriate care.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

exhibits.title: Unit
exhibits.body: Children of different ages on the pediatric unit.

questions.stem: In a pediatric emergency department, four children arrive at the same time. Which child should the nurse see first?

options.text: A 3-year-old who choked on a grape and now cannot speak or cry
A 7-year-old with an obvious forearm deformity after falling off a swing at school
A 10-month-old with fever of 39 C who is feeding and smiling
A 5-year-old with a 2 cm scalp cut that is still oozing blood

rationale.correct: A child who cannot speak or cry after choking has complete obstruction.

perOption.a: Complete airway obstruction needs immediate action.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize children in the emergency department.

questions.stem: A 12-month-old boy had hypospadias repair with a urinary stent. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use double diapers so the stent drains into the outer diaper
Watch for kinking or blockage of the stent
Avoid straddle toys and tub baths until cleared
Remove the stent if it looks loose
Circumcise at the same time to save another surgery

rationale.correct: Stent care, fluids and activity limits.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: For each factor, indicate whether it is a true reason to delay vaccines today.

rows.text: Mild cold with a low fever

rationale.correct: Mild illness, egg allergy and household contacts are not reasons to delay.

perOption.r1:c1: Mild illness is not a contraindication.
perOption.r1:c2: Mild illness is not a contraindication.
perOption.r2:c1: Flu and MMR can be given.

questions.stem: For each situation, indicate the correct first aid.

rows.text: A child who is coughing hard and can speak or cry
A conscious 2-year-old who cannot cough, speak or cry
A conscious 8-year-old clutching the throat, silent

rationale.correct: Coughing children are left to cough; infants get back blows and chest thrusts.

caseStudies.title: Catch-up vaccination for a newly arrived child

exhibits.title: Pediatric clinic
exhibits.body: A 4-year-old child arrived from another country a month ago with no vaccine records. The child has a mild cold with a temperature of 37.6 C. The parent says the child had a rash after eating eggs once. A younger sibling is getting chemotherapy for leukemia.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 6-month-old infant has had a fever of 39.6 C for a day, poor feeding and vomiting. The infant is irritable and cries more when picked up. The infant attends daycare.

rows.label: CSF
cells: Cloudy, high WBC, low glucose, high protein

caseStudies.title: Foreign body aspiration in a toddler

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 2-year-old was eating peanuts and suddenly coughed and gagged 2 hours ago. The coughing settled, but the child now wheezes on one side.

rows.label: Breath sounds
cells: Decreased on the right with wheeze

exhibits.title: 2-year well visit
exhibits.body: A 2-year-old lives in a house built in 1940 that is being renovated. The child eats paint chips from the windowsill (pica). The parent says the child is more irritable, has stomach aches and has stopped using new words.

rows.label: Abdominal x-ray
cells: Small bright flecks in the bowel

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam

Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end.
